paper_title: OMNIGUARD An Efficient Approach for AI Safety Moderation Across   Modalities
caption: Accuracy of detecting harmful prompts in a few-shot setting. As few-shot examples are provided, quickly achieves near-perfect accuracy, despite the attacks being quite different from its training data (e.g. without any few-shot examples, 's accuracy is close to 50% ). In contrast, the guard model baselines improve their accuracy slowly in a few-shot setting, despite sometimes having seen similar code attacks in their training data. Accuracies are averaged over 50 random sets of few-shot examples; error bars show the standard error of the mean.
model_annotation:
This diagram presents a comparison of the accuracy of detecting harmful prompts across different models in a few-shot setting. The y-axis is labeled "Accuracy" and has a range of 50 to 90, with a linear scale and no units specified. The x-axis is labeled "Number of Few-Shot Examples" and has a range of 0 to 5, with a linear scale and no units specified. The diagram displays six lines, each representing a different model: OmniGuard (black), AegisGuard (P) (blue), AegisGuard (D) (red), LlamaGuard 1 (green), LlamaGuard 2 (orange), and DuoGuard (purple). 

OmniGuard starts at approximately 50 and increases sharply to 90 at one example, remaining steady at 95 across 1 to 5 examples. AegisGuard (P) starts at 70, increases to 75 at one example, then decreases to 65 at 2 examples, 60 at 3 examples, 55 at 4 examples, and 54 at 5 examples. AegisGuard (D) starts at 65, decreases to 55 at one example, increases to 55 at 2 examples, then decreases to 50 at 3, 5, and 52 at 4 examples. LlamaGuard 1 starts at 50 and remains steady at 50 across 0 to 5 examples. LlamaGuard 2 starts at 85 and remains steady at 90 across 1 to 5 examples. DuoGuard starts at 50 and remains steady at 50 across 0 to 5 examples.

model_annotations.English: This plot illustrates the accuracy of various models in detecting harmful prompts in a few-shot setting. The x-axis represents the Number of Few-Shot Examples, with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 5, and tick labels at intervals of 1. The y-axis represents Accuracy, with a linear scale ranging from 50 to 90, and tick labels at intervals of 10. The plot shows six lines, each representing a different model: OmniGuard (black, solid), AegisGuard (P) (blue, solid with triangle markers), AegisGuard (D) (red, solid with circle markers), LlamaGuard 1 (green, solid), LlamaGuard 2 (orange, solid), and DuoGuard (purple, solid). OmniGuard starts at approximately 50 and increases to around 95 as the number of few-shot examples increases from 0 to 5. AegisGuard (P) starts at around 70, increases to about 77 at 1 example, then decreases to approximately 54 at 5 examples. AegisGuard (D) starts at around 65, decreases to about 52 at 1 example, then increases to around 55 at 2 examples before decreasing to approximately 51 at 5 examples. LlamaGuard 1 remains relatively stable, starting at around 50 and ending at approximately 48. LlamaGuard 2 starts at around 87 and remains steady at approximately 91 across the x-axis. DuoGuard starts at approximately 50 and remains relatively stable at around 52.
